about.title: About World Zero
about.intro1: World Zero is a community game played in the real world. Players create characters — public personas separate from their login identity — and compete by completing real-world tasks, posting proof of their actions, and earning points through community votes.
about.intro2: Every task has a level requirement. Every submission is rated by the community with a star vote. Points flow from votes; votes flow from participation. The leaderboard reflects not just effort, but community recognition.
about.step1: Sign in with Google and create a Character — your public game persona.
about.step2: Browse open Tasks and sign up for ones that interest you.
about.step3: Complete the task in the real world and post your proof (Praxis).
about.step4: The community votes on submissions with a star rating.
about.step5: Earn points, level up, and unlock new tasks and privileges.
about.inspiredBody: World Zero is inspired by <1>SF0</1>, the original collaborative art game created in San Francisco. SF0 challenged players to complete tasks that blurred the line between game and life. World Zero carries that spirit forward as an open community platform.

donate.title: Support World Zero
donate.intro: World Zero is a community project built and maintained by volunteers. If you enjoy the game and want to help keep it running, consider supporting us on Patreon. Every contribution goes directly toward hosting, development, and keeping the game free for everyone.

settings.title: Settings
settings.lead: Changes save the moment you make them.

account.lead: One account, one email, and however many lives you carry.
account.emailHelp: Where World Zero writes to you. It comes from your sign-in, so it changes there rather than here.
account.providerHelp: World Zero never sees a password — your provider vouches for you each time.

appearance.darkModeHelp: Use the dark palette across every page.
appearance.animationsHelp: Transitions, card hovers, and the level-up celebration. Turn this off to keep the interface still.
appearance.animationsSystemNote: Your device is set to reduce motion.
appearance.animationsSystemName: Animations — off, because your device is set to reduce motion

cookies.lead: This card is the whole policy — there is no separate cookie page. Everything World Zero puts on your device is listed here. None of the switches below is a control: they state what is already true.

essential.title: Essential — required
essential.help: One sign-in cookie, plus the choices your browser remembers for you.
essential.note: Always on. The site cannot sign you in or hold a preference without these.
essential.switchName: Essential storage — always on, because the site cannot sign you in without it

analytics.title: Analytics — never used
analytics.help: Counts of who visits and which pages get used.
analytics.note: Off, and there is nothing behind it: World Zero runs no analytics, no tracking pixels and no third-party scripts.
analytics.switchName: Analytics — off, because World Zero collects none

marketing.title: Marketing — never used
marketing.help: Advertising, ad networks and cross-site tracking.
marketing.note: Off, and there is nothing behind it: World Zero sells nothing and runs no ads.
marketing.switchName: Marketing — off, because World Zero collects none

where.browser: This browser, until you clear it
where.tab: This tab, until you close it

entries.theme: Whether you chose the light or the dark palette.
entries.motion: Whether you asked for animations to stop.
entries.sessionHint: A yes-or-no note that you were signed in last visit, so the likely page can start loading sooner. Never used to decide what you are shown.
entries.adminMode: Whether a moderator left the admin view switched on.
entries.sidebarCollapsed: Whether the side rail is folded away.
entries.sidebarPanels: The order of the side rail's panels and which are folded. One entry for each account signed in on this browser.
entries.factionSections: Which galleries on a faction page you left folded. One entry for each account signed in on this browser.
entries.seenInvites: Which invitation letters a character has already been shown, so none is announced twice. One entry for each of your characters.
entries.lastSeenLevel: The last level a character was congratulated on, so the celebration does not repeat. One entry for each of your characters.
entries.onboardingHandoff: A mark that this tab left for Google or Discord partway through signing up, so you come back where you were.

deletion.title: If you delete your account
deletion.body: Your praxis photos are removed from the disk and your saved composer drafts are emptied. Your name, email, words and pictures are blanked. The votes you cast stay where they are, so nobody else's score moves.
deletion.hash: One thing is kept: which provider you signed in with, and a one-way hash of the ID that provider gave us. The hash cannot be turned back into the ID. It exists so that if you come back we can tell you what happened to your old account, and it is deleted the next time that sign-in returns, once it is more than about ninety days old. Nothing sweeps for one that never returns, so a hash you never come back to can outlive that.

language.lead: English is the only interface language today. Player-written content stays in the language it was written in.
language.requestHelp: Tell us which language you would use. Requests decide what we translate next.
language.requestSent: Thanks — we'll let you know if enough players ask for the same one.
language.requestError: That did not send. Try again in a moment.

data.lead: Download everything tied to your account: your characters, the praxis you posted, the votes you cast, your comments, and the files you uploaded.

export.title: Export my data
export.help: A zip file, built while you wait — nothing is queued and nothing is emailed. Your photos and videos are inside it rather than linked, so the download still makes sense if World Zero is not around.
export.note: If your uploads come to more than 200 MB they are too large to build into one download, and the zip lists a web address for each of them instead. It tells you which of the two you got.
export.failed: That download did not finish. Try it again.
